# A STRESS DOMAIN, NOT AN EXAMPLE — lives under qa/stress_domains/, not
# examples/, on purpose (see qa/bluebook/quality_control.bluebook's own
# "being clever" note and .claude/skills/hecks_qa/SKILL.md's "Authoring a
# new stress domain" section).
#
# TARGETED AT ANGLE-2 (qa/bluebook ledger): reference HOPS, as distinct
# from entity NESTING. `qa/stress_domains/nested_pieces` proves a piece
# inside a piece fuzzes and dispatches correctly, but that is entity
# addressing (`to: { aggregate:, entity: }`); a chain of `reference_to`
# lookups across AGGREGATES goes through a different mechanism entirely —
# `CommandRules::References` (`lib/hecks/runtime/command_rules/
# references.rb`: `resolve_references`, `resolve_state_references`,
# `dereference`) on the write side and `QuerySpecification::HopPath` on
# the read side — and ADR 0037's Finding 5 already named that family as
# the one place Ruby and Rust structurally diverge: `resolve_state_
# references` (the check that walks an AGGREGATE's own reference-typed
# attributes against SETTLED state, after `sets` has copied a command's
# arguments in) was never ported to Rust; only the COMMAND-argument-level
# `resolve_references` was (`rust/project/domain_generator.rb#reference_
# checks`). The ADR closed the finding on the grounds that the corpus's
# one trigger (`SafeDepositBox.Rent` redeclaring `customer` under a plain
# value-object type) had been removed by unrelated work — and said, in
# so many words, "re-open this finding the day one does." This domain
# is that day, deliberately: `Referral.Reassign` below is exactly that
# shape.
#
# EVERY CONSTRUCT HERE IS LOAD-BEARING — the domain is deliberately
# minimal, one aggregate per hop:
#
#   Sponsor  — the far end of every chain (C). Carries the lifecycle
#              field every hop below reads (`standing`), and the ONE
#              role-gated command in the domain (`Suspend`) so the
#              adversary's `role+nonexistent` precedence combination
#              has a reference-carrying, role-carrying command to land on.
#   Member   — one hop from a Sponsor (B → C). `Join`'s `given`
#              dereferences its own `sponsor` argument ONE hop
#              (`sponsor.standing`) — the same shape `Banking::Account.
#              Open`'s `customer.status` already exercises, kept here
#              only because the two-hop chain below has to pass through
#              it. No query of its own: a ONE-hop `where` already exists
#              in banking (`Account.OpenForSuspendedCustomers`) and adds
#              nothing new.
#   Referral — two hops from a Sponsor (A → B → C). `Issue`'s `given`
#              dereferences TWO hops through a fresh argument (`member.
#              sponsor.standing` — `References#dereference` recursing,
#              `DEREFERENCE_DEPTH`); `FromGoodSponsors` is a TWO-hop
#              `where` (`member/sponsor/standing`) — real in Ruby via
#              `HopPath::MAX_HOPS`, a STRUCTURAL skip in Rust (`rust/
#              project/queries.rb`: a where hopping through a reference
#              is "read_model territory" — banking's own one-hop query
#              is skipped the same way, and `query_hop_plan` bails on a
#              second `/` regardless, D2 of the equivalence-gap plan),
#              so the differential harness drops it on both sides and
#              Ruby's own `query_answers_match_reference` property is
#              what checks the answer; and `Reassign` is the ADR 0037
#              Finding 5 shape — see its own comment.
#
# NOT HERE, AND WHY — `has_many`. The first draft of this domain carried
# a fourth aggregate (`Circle`, `has_many Members`, a command supplying
# the list under `list_of(Handle)`) to reach `resolve_state_references`'
# LIST branch. `bin/project_rust` accepted it and emitted Rust that does
# not compile — and because `rust/src/generated/mod.rs` declares every
# generated domain with an unconditional `pub mod`, that broke EVERY
# feature's build, not just this one's. That is this domain's first
# finding, recorded in NOTES.md; the aggregate comes back the day
# codegen can project a `has_many` at all.
#
# `Handle` is redeclared per aggregate rather than shared — this corpus's
# own convention (see waybill.bluebook's `SlotNumber` comment: no chapter
# shares one value object BY NAME across two aggregates without
# redeclaring it locally).
Hecks.bluebook "ReferralChain" do
  vision "A referral is issued by a member, who was sponsored by a sponsor — three aggregates in a reference chain, built to walk every hop the runtime's reference machinery has (a one-hop and a two-hop given, a two-hop where, and a reference re-pointed through a plain value object so only the settled-state check can catch a dangling one) on both engines at once."

  core

  # C — THE FAR END OF EVERY CHAIN. Its `standing` lifecycle field is
  # what every hop below reads through one or two references.
  aggregate "Sponsor" do
    description "Someone who vouches for members; a sponsor in good standing is what makes a referral chain valid."

    identified_by :handle

    attribute :handle, Handle

    value_object "Handle" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a handle is not blank") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :standing, default: "good" do
      transition "Suspend" => "suspended", from: "good"
    end

    command "Enroll" do
      goal "Enroll a sponsor"

      attribute :handle, Handle

      emits "SponsorEnrolled"
    end

    # THE ONE ROLE-GATED COMMAND IN THIS DOMAIN — kept to exactly one on
    # purpose: the adversary's `role+nonexistent` precedence shape needs
    # a command that BOTH declares a role AND addresses an existing
    # record, and nothing else here needs a role to mean anything.
    command "Suspend", from: "good" do
      role "Registrar"
      goal "Suspend a sponsor, invalidating every chain that runs through them"

      reference_to Sponsor

      emits "SponsorSuspended"
    end
  end

  # B — ONE HOP FROM A SPONSOR.
  aggregate "Member" do
    description "Someone a sponsor vouched for; joins under exactly one sponsor."

    identified_by :handle

    attribute :handle, Handle
    reference_to Sponsor

    value_object "Handle" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a handle is not blank") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    command "Join" do
      goal "Join under a sponsor"

      reference_to Sponsor
      attribute :handle, Handle

      # ONE HOP through a fresh argument — `References#dereference`, the
      # same shape `Banking::Account.Open`'s own `customer.status` given.
      given("the sponsor is in good standing") { sponsor.standing == "good" }

      sets :handle
      sets :sponsor

      emits "MemberJoined"
    end
  end

  # A — TWO HOPS FROM A SPONSOR.
  aggregate "Referral" do
    description "A referral a member issues; only valid while the member's own sponsor stands in good standing."

    identified_by :code

    attribute :code, Code
    reference_to Member

    value_object "Code" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a code is not blank") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Handle" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a handle is not blank") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    command "Issue" do
      goal "Issue a referral on behalf of a member"

      reference_to Member
      attribute :code, Code

      # TWO HOPS through a fresh argument — `member` hydrates to the
      # Member's state, whose own `sponsor` hydrates one level further
      # (`dereference`'s own recursion, `DEREFERENCE_DEPTH` = 4). Banking's
      # `Transfer.Request` reads `source.customer.status` the same way.
      given("the member's sponsor is in good standing") { member.sponsor.standing == "good" }

      sets :code
      sets :member

      emits "ReferralIssued"
    end

    # THE ADR 0037 FINDING 5 SHAPE, RE-OPENED ON PURPOSE. `member` is
    # REDECLARED here under `Handle` — a plain value object, not the
    # aggregate's own `Reference<Member>` — so the command-level
    # `resolve_references` (the one check Rust ported) sees no reference
    # at all: `reference?` is false on the command's own attribute.
    # `sets :member` then copies the handle straight into the aggregate's
    # reference field, and only `resolve_state_references` (Ruby,
    # `step_save`, walking `Referral.member`'s real `Reference<Member>`
    # type against the SETTLED state) asks whether it names a Member
    # that exists. This is `SafeDepositBox.Rent`'s pre-#409 shape, byte
    # for byte in spirit — the trigger the ADR's own closing note said
    # to re-open the finding for.
    command "Reassign" do
      goal "Re-point a referral at a different member, by handle"

      reference_to Referral
      attribute :member, Handle

      sets :member

      emits "ReferralReassigned"
    end

    # TWO-HOP WHERE — real in Ruby (`HopPath::MAX_HOPS`), a structural
    # refusal in Rust ("is not generated for this domain" — see the
    # header comment). The differential harness drops it on both sides;
    # Ruby's own `query_answers_match_reference` property is what checks
    # the answer, and the structural skip itself is what PR-2's skip
    # reporting exists to surface.
    query "FromGoodSponsors" do
      description "Referrals whose issuing member's sponsor is in good standing."
      where(:"member/sponsor/standing" => "good")
      order_by :code
    end
  end
end
